questions.question: Sarcomere is the area between -
questions.explanation:
Sarcomere
A sarcomere is the region between two successive Z-lines (Z-discs) in a myofibril.

questions.question:

actin and are called
questions.explanation:
The light bands of a muscle fibre contain thin actin filaments and are called the I-bands (Isotropic bands). ✅



I-band → Actin → Light

A-band → Myosin + Actin overlap → Dark

questions.question:
The cross bridges of the sarcomere in
skeletal muscle are made up of –
questions.explanation:
The cross-bridges in the sarcomere of skeletal muscle are made up of myosin. ✅

Specifically, they are the globular heads of myosin molecules.

Myosin head = Cross-bridge → binds actin → ATPase activity → muscle contraction.

questions.question:
The functions of tropomyosin in skeletal
muscle include
questions.option_a: Sliding on actin to produceshortening
questions.option_b: Release Ca+2 after initiation ofcontraction
questions.option_c: Acting as "relaxing protein" at rest bycovering up the sites where myosinbinds to actin
questions.explanation:
Functions of Tropomyosin in skeletal muscle

Tropomyosin is a regulatory protein associated with actin (thin filament).

Its main functions are:

1. At rest: Covers the myosin-binding sites on actin, preventing actin–myosin interaction.


2. During contraction: In the presence of Ca²⁺, tropomyosin shifts away from the binding sites, allowing myosin heads to bind actin.


Tropomyosin = blocks actin–myosin binding at rest.
Ca²⁺ + troponin → tropomyosin moves → contraction starts.

questions.question:
Ca+2 bind _________ in the skeletal
muscles and leads to exposure of the
binding site for _______ on the filament
_________
questions.explanation:
Ca²⁺ binds to troponin in skeletal muscle and leads to exposure of the binding site for myosin on the filament actin. 

Troponin → Myosin → Actin

Ca²⁺ → Troponin → Tropomyosin shifts → Myosin-binding sites on Actin exposed.

questions.question:
The action potential that triggers a
muscle contraction travels deep within
the muscle cell by means of _________.
questions.explanation:
The action potential that triggers skeletal muscle contraction travels deep into the muscle fibre through T-tubules (transverse tubules). 

📌 Answer: T-tubules

They carry the action potential from the sarcolemma deep into the muscle fibre, triggering Ca²⁺ release from the sarcoplasmic reticulum.

questions.question:
ATP provides energy for muscle
contraction by allowing for-
questions.option_a: An action potential formation in themuscle cell
questions.option_b: Cross-bridge detachment of myosinfrom actin
questions.option_c: Cross-bridge attachment of myosin toactin
questions.option_d: Release of ca+2 from sarcoplasmicreticulum
questions.explanation:
ATP provides energy for muscle contraction mainly by allowing myosin heads to detach from actin and then re-cock into their high-energy position.


ATP binds to myosin → myosin detaches from actin.
Then ATP hydrolysis provides energy to re-cock the myosin head for the next power stroke.
